name: MAX490EESA+T
title: MAX481E/MAX483E/MAX485E/MAX487E–MAX491E/MAX1487E: low-power RS-485/RS-422 transceivers with ±15 kV ESD protection on the bus pins, full-speed or slew-limited
summary: A family of nine 5 V RS-485/RS-422 transceivers, each with one driver and one receiver, whose bus pins withstand ±15 kV Human Body Model ESD. Five are full speed (2.5 Mbps) and four slew limited (250 kbps); five are half duplex on one pair and four (MAX488E to MAX491E) full duplex on two. MAX490E is the 8-pin full-duplex, 2.5 Mbps part with no enables, drawing 300 µA typical. Drivers are current limited and have thermal shutdown; the receiver output goes high with its inputs open.

circuits.title: Typical half-duplex link (MAX481E/MAX483E/MAX485E/MAX487E/MAX1487E)
circuits.description: One transceiver at each end of a single twisted pair. The local part U1 has its supply bypassed by 0.1 µF and puts its driver and receiver on the same pair, A and B. The pair is terminated at both ends by Rt across A and B, one at U1 and one at the far transceiver U2. DE and RE at each end choose which station talks and which listens.

parts.note: line termination at the far end

notes: Where the timing and test figures name Y and Z, these parts use A and B (with DE high).

circuits.title: Typical full-duplex link (MAX488E/MAX490E)
circuits.description: Two twisted pairs, one for each direction. U1's driver sends on Y and Z to the far receiver, and U1's receiver listens on A and B to the far driver. Each pair carries a termination Rt at its receiving end: across A and B at U1, across the Y-Z pair at the far transceiver U2. U1's supply pin has a 0.1 µF bypass capacitor.

termination of the Y-Z pair at the far end

circuits.title: Typical full-duplex link with enables (MAX489E/MAX491E)
circuits.description: The 14-pin full-duplex parts in the same two-pair link: U1 drives the Y-Z pair and receives on the A-B pair, each pair terminated by Rt at its receiving end. DE and RE give separate control of U1's driver and receiver, and the far transceiver U2 has its own DE and RE. Both GND pins go to ground, the three N.C. pins are left open, and VCC has a 0.1 µF bypass capacitor.

circuits.title: Half-duplex RS-485 network (MAX481E/MAX483E/MAX485E/MAX487E/MAX1487E)
circuits.description: Four transceivers share one twisted pair, A to A and B to B. The two stations at the ends of the cable, U1 and U4, each have a 120 Ω resistor across A and B; the stations between them tap the pair with no termination. Each station keeps its own DI, DE, RO and RE; only one driver may be enabled at a time.

circuits.title: Full-duplex RS-485 network (MAX488E–MAX491E)
circuits.description: A master and three slaves on two pairs. The master U1 drives one pair from Y and Z, which every slave receives on its A and B; every slave drives the other pair from Y and Z, which the master receives on A and B. Both pairs are terminated with 120 Ω at the master and again at the far end of the cable.

across the B-A pair at the far end

notes: RE and DE exist only on MAX489E and MAX491E.

circuits.description: The driver output under test carries CL to ground and a 500 Ω resistor to a node that switch S1 ties to VCC or switch S2 ties to ground.

circuits.description: A TTL signal with edges under 6 ns drives DI. The driver's Z output goes to the receiver's B input and Y to A; 54 Ω lies across the pair and each line has 100 pF to ground. RO is the receiver output being timed.

operation.text: Nine single-driver, single-receiver RS-485/RS-422 transceivers on one 5 V supply. MAX481E, MAX485E, MAX490E, MAX491E and MAX1487E have full-speed drivers good to 2.5 Mbps; MAX483E, MAX487E, MAX488E and MAX489E have slew-limited drivers rated to 250 kbps. MAX488E to MAX491E are full duplex with separate driver and receiver pins; the others are half duplex on one A-B pair. Each is the bus-pin ESD-hardened version of the part of the same number without the E, with the same pins and functions.
MAX490E: full duplex, 2.5 Mbps, drivers not slew limited, no shutdown, no driver or receiver enable, 300 µA quiescent current, a standard unit-load receiver (32 transceivers on a bus), 8 pins.

MAX481E, MAX483E, MAX485E, MAX487E, MAX489E, MAX491E and MAX1487E have a driver enable DE and an active-low receiver enable RE; disabled outputs are high impedance. MAX488E and MAX490E have neither: the driver and the receiver are always on.
With the receiver inputs open, RO goes high.
Quiescent current is as low as 120 µA, unloaded or loaded with the drivers disabled. MAX481E, MAX483E and MAX487E also have a shutdown mode at 0.5 µA typical.

MAX481E, MAX483E and MAX487E shut down when RE is high and DE is low together; with either the driver or the receiver enabled they stay awake. RE and DE may change at the same moment: a state held under 50 ns never causes shutdown, one held 600 ns or more always does. The other operating combinations of RE, DE (0,1; 1,1; 0,0) keep the part in normal mode. MAX485E, MAX488E to MAX491E and MAX1487E have no shutdown. Waking from shutdown takes longer than enabling from normal mode: tZH(SHDN) and tZL(SHDN) apply after shutdown, tZH and tZL when the part was awake.

Two mechanisms limit fault and bus-contention current. A foldback current limit in the output stage protects against shorts anywhere in the common-mode range at once, and a thermal shutdown switches the driver outputs to high impedance if the die gets too hot.

The slew-limited drivers of MAX483E and MAX487E to MAX489E lower EMI and reflections from poorly terminated cable. Transmitting a 150 kHz signal, the full-speed parts show large high-frequency harmonics in the output spectrum; the slew-limited parts show much smaller ones. The slew-limited parts tolerate imperfect termination better.

MAX487E and MAX1487E have a 48 kΩ, quarter-unit-load receiver input and allow 128 transceivers on a bus. MAX481E, MAX483E, MAX485E and MAX488E to MAX491E have the standard 12 kΩ input, one unit load, for 32 transceivers.

Receiver skew |tPLH - tPHL| is typically under 13 ns on MAX481E, MAX485E, MAX490E, MAX491E and MAX1487E and under 100 ns on MAX483E and MAX487E to MAX489E. Driver skew is typically 5 ns (10 ns max) on the fast parts and 100 ns (800 ns max) on the slew-limited ones.

All pins have ESD structures for handling and assembly. The bus pins (A, B, Y, Z) are characterized to ±15 kV with the Human Body Model, in normal operation, in shutdown and powered down, and keep working afterwards without latchup. External transient suppressors, with their capacitance, are not needed.

Human Body Model: 100 pF charged to the test voltage through a 1 MΩ charging resistor and discharged into the device through 1.5 kΩ. IEC1000-4-2: 150 pF, charged through 50 MΩ to 100 MΩ, discharged through 330 Ω; its current rises in 0.7 ns to 1 ns and its peak is higher, so withstand voltages measured this way are usually lower than by the Human Body Model. IEC1000-4-2 has contact-discharge and air-gap methods. Machine Model: 200 pF with no discharge resistance, applied to all pins, relevant mainly to manufacturing.
Each end of the line carries a termination equal to the cable's characteristic impedance, and stubs off the main line are kept as short as possible. Bypass VCC with 0.1 µF.
RS-485/RS-422 covers lines up to 4000 ft. The parts can also serve as line repeaters for longer cables.
